nextStoryContext: US-R1-005 fixed the WARNING that US-R1-004's config-pane debug log EXIT-trap cleanup (buildConfigLogCleanupCommand, src/commands/setup.ts) raced the cap's rotate loop (buildConfigLogCapCommand): the trap fired `tmux pipe-pane -t $PANE` (a synchronous RPC that only ASKS tmux to close the pipe, returns immediately) directly followed by `rm -f $LOG $LOG.chunk` on the next line, while the piped writer -- a separate process spawned by tmux in the viewer sub-pane, never a child of the menu script that owns the trap -- could still be mid-flight finishing its current chunk's `cat >> LOG` or `tail -c ... && mv ... LOG` rotate. If that pending mv landed after the rm, the log file was recreated after cleanup and survived the menu exit (AC8's 'removed on menu exit with no residue'). Fix: buildConfigLogCapCommand now creates a `.lock` sibling as its very first action and removes it (with the .chunk scratch file) as its very last action, strictly after its own loop has broken on EOF -- a single-process ordering guarantee needing no cross-process sync primitive on the writer's side. buildConfigLogCleanupCommand still asks tmux to close the pipe first, but now polls (bounded: 40 tries at 0.05s apart, ~2s worst case) for that `.lock` to disappear BEFORE its own `rm -f LOG CHUNK LOCK`, sequencing the removal strictly after the writer's last write instead of racing it. When no writer is (or ever was) running, the lock never existed, the poll loop's condition is false on the very first check, and cleanup is exactly as fast as before (asserted explicitly with an elapsedMs < 500ms check on that path, so the fix can't silently regress into always paying the poll cost). Verified non-tautological: stashed this story's src/commands/setup.ts fix (kept the new composed test file changes) and re-ran the two new composed tests against the pre-fix buildConfigLogCleanupCommand from HEAD -- both failed (cleanup returned while the simulated writer's lock was still held; a real-writer-plus-real-cleanup end-to-end race left LOG/.chunk/.lock residue on disk) -- then restored the fix and confirmed both pass, alongside all 9 pre-existing tests in that file (11/11 total, up from the prior handoff's implied 9). The two prior halves (buildConfigLogCapCommand, buildConfigLogCleanupCommand) were previously only ever tested in isolation (one always ran with CAM_CONFIG_PANE="", i.e. no real writer in flight); this story adds a new 'EXIT-trap teardown vs writer rotate race (US-R1-005)' describe block that composes both real snippets end-to-end under real bash, plus a deterministic timing-controlled simulated-lock test that proves the wait is genuine (not a no-op) without relying on hard-to-reproduce real-world scheduling luck. file-size-budget.json raised for src/commands/setup.ts 978->1017 with a dated US-R1-005/CAM-510 _ref note (the gate's own reported line count, not wc -l, per the file-size rubric). All quality gates green: typecheck 0 errors, full bun test 6099 pass / 0 fail (+3 from the new tests, up from the 6096 baseline recorded in the prior handoff), full bun run check:all spine green (file-size, debt-markers, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, test-tmpdir, skip-ratchet). No vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. Step 5.5 fetched the current tmux(1) manpage to confirm `pipe-pane` with no shell-command argument closes any existing pipe -- confirms the EOF-on-toggle-off assumption the fix (and the prior US-R1-004 site-4 fix) both rely on. This closes the last known CAM-510 site-4 follow-up finding against this branch's prior work; CAM-513 (flaky-test-isolation, filed on main from US-R1-003) remains open, unrelated to this story's diff.
